diagnosis_explanation: Your body had a problem with a pregnancy. It started growing in the wrong place. This caused bleeding inside your belly. You also had blood loss. This made your blood count low.
medication_rationale:
Pain Medication (new):
This medicine is given to help with your pain.
It will make you feel more comfortable.
You may feel sleepy or groggy. This is normal.
Call your doctor if your pain gets worse.
Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.

Iron Therapy (new):
This medicine is to help your body make more red blood cells.
You lost blood and your body needs help to replace it.
Your stools may turn black. This is normal.
Call your doctor if you get bad stomach pain.
Call your doctor if you vomit blood.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will feel tired and sore after surgery.
- You will have some pain around your incision.
- You can do light activities inside your home.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 10 pounds.
- Walk a little bit each day.
- Your goal is to walk to your mailbox.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101°F.
- Call your doctor if you have heavy vaginal bleeding.

**Week 2:**
- Your pain should start to get better.
- You will still feel tired but may have more energy.
- You can increase your walking distance slowly.
- Continue to avoid lifting anything heavier than 10 pounds.
- Eat regular meals.
- Your goal is to walk for 10 minutes twice a day.
- Call your doctor if you have bad nausea or vomiting.

**Week 3:**
- You should feel more comfortable moving around.
- You may be able to do light chores.
- Continue to avoid heavy lifting or strenuous exercise.
- You can likely walk for longer periods now.
- Your goal is to walk for 15 minutes each day.
- Call your doctor if your incision starts to look red or swollen.

**Week 4:**
- Most days should feel easier than the week before.
- You can likely resume most normal daily activities.
- You may return to work if your job is not strenuous.
- Continue to avoid heavy lifting for a few more weeks.
- Your goal is to walk for 20 minutes each day.
- Call your doctor if you have any new or worsening pain.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Your energy levels will gradually increase.
- Pain will continue to decrease each week.
- You should feel back to your normal self in 4 to 6 weeks.
- Healing is a process, so be patient with your body.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Severe pain in your belly: This could be bleeding inside.
- Dizziness or fainting: You may be losing too much blood.
- Fast heart rate and pale skin: Your body needs blood flow.
- Feeling like you will pass out: This means your blood pressure is low.
- Bleeding more than a period: This is not normal for you.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Mild belly pain that worsens: Keep an eye on your pain.
- Feeling weak or very tired: You lost blood and need to rest.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Questions about your pain medicine: Your doctor can help you manage pain.
- Questions about your iron pills: Your doctor can check your iron levels.
